# Volume 1 — CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

THIRZA advanced with a brisk step the moment Obed swung the door open. However, upon catching sight of the peculiar, small form wearing the rigid, unattractive garment, possessing extended plaits of crimson hair alongside keen, shining eyes, she halted abruptly, thoroughly astonished.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0000 }

“Obed Abernethy, who is that?” she blurted out. “Where can the boy be?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0001 }

“No boy existed,” Obed stated in misery. “She was the only one.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0002 }

He gave the girl a nod, recalling that he had not once inquired what she was called.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0003 }

“No boy! However, a boy had to be there,” Thirza declared firmly. “Word was sent by us for Mrs. Tranter to bring a boy along.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0004 }

“Indeed, she failed to do so. The girl was brought by her. This was confirmed by my query to the stationmaster. Consequently, bringing her back fell upon me. Leaving her at that place was impossible, regardless of how the error originated.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0005 }

“Indeed, what a fine mess we have here!” Thirza exclaimed.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0006 }

Throughout this conversation the girl had stayed quiet, her gaze shifting between the two of them as every bit of liveliness drained from her features. Instantly, she appeared to understand the complete significance of their words. Letting her treasured carpet-bag fall, she leaped a stride ahead and folded her hands together.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0007 }

“I am not wanted by you!” she exclaimed. “My not being a boy is why you don’t want me! It should have been anticipated by me. Me, nobody ever wanted. That it was all far too lovely to endure ought to have been known to me. That truly nobody wanted me should have been known to me. Oh, what am I to do? Tears are going to burst from me!”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0008 }

She broke down into weeping. Dropping onto a seat beside the table, throwing her arms across its surface, and hiding her face within them, she began to sob turbulently. Thirza and Obed exchanged apologetic glances over the stove. Both were at a loss regarding what to speak or perform. At last, Thirza clumsily took action to handle the situation.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0009 }

“Indeed, indeed, crying like that over it is quite unnecessary.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0010 }

“Indeed, I must!” Instantly lifting her face, the little girl showed moist cheeks and quivering lips. “If you were a parentless child who arrived at a spot expected to be your home, only to discover you were undesired for not being a male, you would weep as well. Oh, my life has never known a more calamitous event!”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0011 }

A expression resembling a hesitant smile, somewhat stiff from extended inactivity, softened the stern look on Thirza’s face.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0012 }

“Well, stop crying now. You will not be cast out-of-doors by us tonight. Staying here will be necessary for you until this affair is investigated by us. What is your name?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0013 }

The young one paused briefly.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0014 }

“Would you be so kind as to address me as Lucinda?” she asked with enthusiasm.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0015 }

“Is Lucinda what you are called? Does that name belong to you?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0016 }

“Na-a-ay, that isn’t quite what I am called, though I’d adore having Lucinda as a name. That name possesses such complete elegance.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0017 }

“I have no idea what you are talking about. What is your name, if it isn’t Lucinda?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0018 }

“Nell Harcourt,” the person bearing that name hesitatingly admitted, “yet, oh, I beg you to address me as Lucinda. What name you use for me cannot be of great importance to you if my stay is to be merely brief, can it? Besides, Nell is a name so lacking in romance.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0019 }

“Unromantic fiddlesticks!” declared the unfeeling Thirza. “Nell is a truly excellent, simple, and practical name. There is no reason for you to feel embarrassed by it.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0020 }

“Oh, I’m not ashamed of it,” Nell explained, “only Lucinda is better to my liking. I’ve always pictured my name being Lucinda—at least, I always have in recent years. When I was young I used to picture it being Seraphine, but Lucinda is more to my liking now. But if you call me Nell please call me Nell spelled with an E.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0021 }

“Does the spelling really matter?” Thirza inquired, another creaky smile appearing as her hand reached for the teapot.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0022 }

“Oh, that alters everything so much. Its appearance is far prettier. Doesn't a name always appear before your eyes, exactly as though it were written down, whenever someone says it aloud? Mine does; and while A-n-n seems terrible, A-n-n-e strikes one as far more refined. Should you merely agree to address me as Nell with an E added, I will endeavor to accept that I am not named Lucinda.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0023 }

“Is it possible for you, Nell with an E at the end, to explain how this error occurred? Our message to Mrs. Tranter requested that a boy be brought to us. Was the asylum completely lacking in boys?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0024 }

“Oh, yes, there were plenty of them. However, Mrs. Tranter stated clearly that a girl around eleven years of age was what you desired. And the matron mentioned she believed I would fit the description. You cannot imagine how happy I felt. Joy kept me awake the entire night before. Oh,” she remarked accusingly, looking toward Obed, “why failed you to inform me at the depot that I was unwanted and abandon me at that place? Had I not observed the Petal Road of Delight and the Lake of Glassy Waters, this would be less difficult.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0025 }

“Whatever could she possibly imply?” asked Thirza, looking directly at Obed.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0026 }

“She—she is merely mentioning a discussion we took part in along the way,” Obed said hurriedly. “I am heading outside to hitch up the mare, Thirza. Ensure tea is prepared for my return.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0027 }

“Was anyone else brought over by Mrs. Tranter besides you?” Thirza asked further after Obed had departed.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0028 }

“She acquired Lily Jones for her own. Lily has reached just five years of age and is extremely beautiful, possessing nut-brown hair. Were I extremely beautiful with nut-brown hair, would you retain me?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0029 }

“No. A boy is what we need to assist Obed on the farm. To us, a girl would be useless. Remove your hat. On the hall table, I’ll place it along with your bag.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0030 }

Nell submissively removed her headwear. Shortly after, Obed returned, and the two of them sat for their evening meal. However, eating proved impossible for Nell. She attempted to chew on the bread and butter and sampled the crab-apple preserve from the small, scalloped glass bowl beside her place setting, yet it was all to no purpose. She truly failed to progress whatsoever.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0031 }

“You are taking no food at all,” Thirza remarked in a stern tone, observing her as though this indicated a major defect. A sigh escaped from Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0032 }

“I am unable to. Despair has completely consumed me. Is it possible for you to consume food when you are completely consumed by despair?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0033 }

“Having never experienced the lowest depths of hopelessness, I am unable to tell,” replied Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0034 }

“Were you not? Well, did you ever attempt to picture yourself in the bottom of hopelessness?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0035 }

“No, I didn’t.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0036 }

“In that case, I doubt you are able to grasp how it feels. It is truly a most unpleasant sensation. Whenever you attempt to eat, a lump rises straight into your throat and swallowing becomes impossible, even if you were offered a chocolate caramel. A single chocolate caramel was given to me once two years ago, and its taste was wonderful. Since that time, I have frequently dreamed of possessing many chocolate caramels, yet awakening always occurs at the exact moment I am about to consume them. It is my sincere wish that you will not take offense at my inability to eat. All of this is exceptionally lovely, and yet I am unable to eat.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0037 }

“She seems exhausted to me,” remarked Obed, breaking his silence since coming back from the barn. “You ought to put her to bed, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0038 }

Thirza had pondered which bed Nell ought to occupy. For the hoped-for and anticipated male child, she had made up a sofa located in the kitchen room. Yet, despite its tidy and spotless state, placing a female child there felt somehow inappropriate. On the other hand, offering the guest bedroom to a mere homeless orphan was completely impossible, leaving the room in the east gable as the sole option. Thirza set fire to a candle wick and instructed Nell to come after her, a command Nell obeyed without energy, picking up her head covering and luggage off the hall table along the way. That hallway possessed a daunting cleanliness; the small gable bedroom where she soon ended up appeared even more immaculate.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0039 }

Thirza placed the light upon a triangular table with three legs and folded back the bedding.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0040 }

“I take it you own a nightgown?” she asked.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0041 }

Nell gave a nod.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0042 }

“Indeed, I possess two. They were crafted for me by the matron at the asylum. They are terribly scant. Because an asylum never has sufficient supplies to distribute, items are invariably scant—or at least that is the case in an impoverished asylum such as ours. Scant night-dresses are something I despise. Nevertheless, it is possible to dream equally well inside them as inside beautiful sweeping ones that feature neck frills, which serves as a single comfort.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0043 }

“Now, strip off your clothes as fast as possible and get into bed. In a little while, I’ll return to fetch the candle. Leaving you to extinguish it on your own is too risky. It’s probable you’d burn down the house.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0044 }

After Thirza departed, Nell gazed about herself mournfully. So agonizingly plain and bright were the whitewashed walls that she believed they had to hurt from their own plainness. Likewise, the floor was uncarpeted, save for a central circular braided mat unlike any Nell had previously encountered. The bed, an elevated, antique model featuring four dark, shortly turned posts, occupied one corner. The previously mentioned triangular table was situated in the opposite corner, decorated by a chubby, red velvet pincushion sufficiently firm to bend the tip of even the boldest pin. A small six-by-eight mirror was suspended above it. Located halfway between the table and the bed was the window, covered by a frozen white muslin frill, while the wash-stand sat across from it. The entire room possessed an indescribable stiffness that chilled Nell to the deep center of her bones. Weeping, she rapidly removed her clothes, donned the tight nightgown, and leaped into bed, where she dug face down into the pillow and dragged the covers above her head. When Thirza returned upstairs to fetch the light, several meager pieces of clothing strewn very carelessly across the floor and a particular chaotic look to the bed served as the sole signs that anyone besides herself was there.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0045 }

She intentionally gathered the garments belonging to Nell, laid them orderly upon a stiff yellow chair, and afterwards, carrying the candle, walked across to the bed.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0046 }

“Good night,” she spoke, somewhat stiffly, yet with a degree of warmth.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0047 }

With a suddenness that was startling, Nell’s pale face and large eyes emerged above the bedding.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0048 }

“In what way is it possible for you to term the night good, given your awareness that it has to be the most terrible one I have ever experienced?” she asked in a tone of reproach.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0049 }

Afterward, she descended below sight once more.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0050 }

Thirza walked leisurely down toward the kitchen, where she began cleaning the dishes from supper. Obed was engaged in smoking, which served as a clear indication that his mind was troubled. He rarely used tobacco, since Thirza firmly opposed it on the grounds that it was a disgusting practice; however, on particular occasions and in certain circumstances, he felt compelled to do so, and Thirza would deliberately ignore the behavior during those moments, recognizing that an ordinary man requires some outlet to release his feelings.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0051 }

“Well, this is a fine mess,” she declared angrily. “That is the result of dispatching a message rather than traveling there in person. The family of Richard Tranter has altered that news in some manner. It is definite that a person among us must travel by carriage to visit Mrs. Tranter the following day. This child must be returned to the orphanage.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0052 }

“Yes, I guess that is right,” Obed admitted with hesitation.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0053 }

“You believe that is the case! Is it not a certainty to you?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0054 }

“Indeed, Thirza is quite a lovely young girl. Since she is so eager to remain with us, returning her seems rather unfortunate.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0055 }

“Obed Abernethy, surely you are not suggesting that we should retain her!”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0056 }

Thirza could not have been more astonished if Obed had declared a preference for standing on his head.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0057 }

“I don't imagine we do—at least, not entirely,” Obed faltered, trapped uneasily while attempting to clarify his exact intention. “It seems to me—it would scarcely be reasonable for us to retain her.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0058 }

“I would think not. Of what use could she possibly be to us?”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0059 }

“We could perhaps render her some assistance,” Obed remarked abruptly and out of the blue.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0060 }

“Obed Abernethy, my belief is that you have been enchanted by that child! It is as clear as day to me that your desire is to retain her.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0061 }

“Well now, she is a truly fascinating young lady,” Obed continued. “If only you had listened to her speaking on the way from the station.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0062 }

“Oh, her tongue moves quickly enough. That was immediately obvious to me. Furthermore, it counts against her. Children with so much to say are not to my liking. An orphan girl is not what I want, and even if she were, I would not choose her type. About her, there is something I fail to comprehend. No, she must be sent back without delay to the place she originated from.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0063 }

“A French boy could be hired by me for assistance,” Obed said, “and you would have her for company.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0064 }

“Company is not something I am lacking,” Thirza replied abruptly. “Furthermore, keeping her is not my intention.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0065 }

“Indeed, Thirza, things are precisely as you describe,” Obed remarked while standing up and stowing his pipe. “I am retiring for the night.”
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0066 }

Obed retired to bed. Thirza likewise retired to bed, a look of utmost determination on her face, after storing her dishes. Meanwhile, on an upper floor within the east gable, a little girl who was solitary, starving for affection, and devoid of friends wept until sleep took her.
{: #nw-v01-c03-p0067 }
